title: Relationships between Hong Kong statutory documents for architects
description: How the instruments in hk_s_reference relate. Legal force runs from ordinance to regulation to an accepted code of practice to a practice note. A government lease and the site outline zoning plan can be stricter than the Buildings Ordinance. Practice notes state how the authority applies the law. They do not replace it.

diagrams.title: Legal force
diagrams.description: Strongest instrument first. A Code of Practice is a method the Building Authority has accepted. A practice note explains that application. BEAM Plus (Building Environmental Assessment Method Plus) is a voluntary assessment and sits outside this chain.
diagrams.accessibility: Ordinance authorizes a subsidiary regulation, which an accepted code of practice applies, which a practice note explains. A government lease and a site outline zoning plan can be stricter than the Buildings Ordinance. BEAM Plus is voluntary.

diagrams.title: Two different licences
diagrams.description: Cap 408, the Architects Registration Ordinance, controls the title Registered Architect through the Architects Registration Board. It does not approve building plans. An Authorized Person is a separate registration with the Building Authority under Cap 123, the Buildings Ordinance.
diagrams.accessibility: Cap 408 leads to the Registered Architect title and does not approve plans. Separate Building Authority registration creates an Authorized Person, who submits and supervises under Cap 123.

diagrams.title: Cap 123 and its subsidiary regulations
diagrams.description: Cap 121, the Buildings Ordinance (Application to the New Territories) Ordinance, decides how Cap 123 applies in the New Territories. Cap 123B, the Building (Construction) Regulations, is the earlier construction text. Use it when a project still cites that text. Cap 123Q, the Building (Construction) Regulation, is the later construction regulation.
diagrams.accessibility: Cap 123 is the parent ordinance. Cap 121 limits its application in the New Territories. The lettered regulations cover administration, planning, construction, energy, sanitation, refuse, minor works, inspection, and other specialist duties.

diagrams.title: How the Building Authority applies Cap 123
diagrams.description: Practice Notes for Authorized Persons and Joint Practice Notes state how the Building Authority applies the ordinance. Joint Practice Notes 4, 5, 6 and 7 change gross floor area, height, setback and site coverage. Joint Practice Note 8 is the statutory gross floor area effect of modular integrated construction.
diagrams.accessibility: Administration notes govern submission. Planning notes and joint practice notes govern area and form. The fire, access, supervision and energy codes are the accepted methods under the matching regulation.

diagrams.title: What actually limits the site
diagrams.description: A master schedule of Notes is a standard form. It is not the site Outline Zoning Plan. The Hong Kong Planning Standards and Guidelines are guidance. On a real site, the site plan, its Notes, and the government lease control the envelope and can be tighter than Cap 123.
diagrams.accessibility: Cap 123, the site outline zoning plan, and the government lease all feed the site envelope. The master schedule and the planning standards do not replace the site plan.

diagrams.title: Regimes that sit beside Cap 123
diagrams.description: These ordinances can still constrain a scheme after the Buildings Ordinance is satisfied. Lease control is in the previous diagram. Cap 610, the Buildings Energy Efficiency Ordinance, is the building-services energy code. It is not Cap 123M, which is the overall thermal transfer value regime. Cap 618, the Lifts and Escalators Ordinance, is administered with the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department, alongside Cap 123D and Cap 123E.
diagrams.accessibility: A scheme that meets Cap 123 still faces planning, fire services, pollution, airport height, existing-building fire safety, energy, lifts, water, labour safety, and antiquities controls.

diagrams.title: Path from appointment to occupation permit
diagrams.description: The statutory job under Cap 123. The Authorized Person, Registered Structural Engineer, Registered Geotechnical Engineer and registered contractor are appointed first. Section 14 is approval and consent. Section 16 is refusal. Section 21 is the occupation permit. Fire Services Department acceptance of fire service installations is a parallel gate. It is not itself the occupation permit.
diagrams.accessibility: Appointment leads to plan submission, then section 14 consent or section 16 refusal. Consent leads through supervision and completion to the section 21 occupation permit. Fire services acceptance runs beside completion.
